captopril therapy decreases the expression and function of the alpha(1D) subtype of alpha-adrenoceptor in the aorta of pre- hypertensive rats.
Captopril therapy decreased both expression and function alpha(1D) adrenoceptors in pre-hypetensive rat aorta.

the effects of captopri therapy on the expression and function of the different alpha(1)-subtype adrenoceptors.
a better understanding of the mechanisms by which the ACE inhibitors exert a protective effect against the development of hypertension and its associated cardiovascular complications.
the effects of ACE inhibition on alpha(1)adrenoceptor expression and function in aorta of SHR.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of captoppril on alpha(1D) adrenoceptor mRNA and function are not mediated by a decrease of angiotensinin II synthesis.
the effects of captoppril on alpha(1D) adrenoceptor mRNA and alpha(1D)/alpha(1A) adrenoceptor protein expression in pre-hypetensive rats is not a direct effect but is mediated via angiotensin-II.

the ACE-inhibition by captopril decreases both expression and contractile response of alpha(1)-subtype of adrenoceptors in pre-hypetensive rat aorta, which could be an important mechanism of action of captopril in the treatment of hypertension and heart failure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
captopril therapy in pre-hypetensive rats decreases alpha(1)-subtype expression and function, probably through blockade of the angiotensin-II synthesis.
captopril therapy decreases both the expression and function of the alpha(1D) subtype in pre-hypetensive SHR.
captopril treatment decreases alpha(1D) mRNA and protein in SHR aorta, but increases alpha(1D)mRNA in WKY.

captopril therapy decreases both the expression and function of the alpha-adrenoceptors.
